heading: Analysis & comparisons
title: Analysis title
finishReference: Use or cancel the open reference selection before saving.
changedSample: The first 20 changed sources are shown. All changed sources require the same applicability review.
unavailable: Unrecorded identities and why they are unavailable
name: Parameter name
invalid: Complete the analysis identity, uncertainty, limitations and source mappings. Use explicit unknowns where evidence is unavailable.
source: Use declared source order within each source and context
expectedHelp: Optional: choose a separately retained expected table. Rows are compared in order by exact key and exact value, with matching units. Unmatched keys, absent rows and exclusions remain visible. A matching fixture does not establish instrument accuracy or independence; describe its origin.
intro: Map retained results without rewriting observations. Categories describe supplied assessments. Boundary views never change acceptance bands. Missing values do not count as successful observations; aggregate rows are kept separate from raw readings.
mappingHelp: Optional columns override the context declared below. Membership uses unspecified, calibration, training or held-out; window relationship uses unknown, disjoint or overlapping; observation basis uses raw or aggregate. Unknown category spellings stop preparation.
jobHelp: Preparation runs in the workspace worker. Close this dialog and return from Evidence & analysis to check it, cancel or retry. Earlier revisions remain available.
denominatorHelp: Successful / assessed counts include only raw correct and mismatched observations. Other categories are reported separately. Repeated readings are not independent runs. Aggregate denominators are source declarations and are never automatically pooled.
causality: Order and co-occurrence are descriptive. No causal relationship or clock conversion is inferred. Transitions require declared source order and never cross source/context boundaries.
changed: Inputs changed or became unavailable. Retained results and source revisions remain unchanged; review their applicability.
figureUnlinked: Authored presentation: values are retained in this record's data table. A supporting result, sources and interpretation limits have not been declared.
resultHelp: Identify authored statements explicitly or pin a retained analysis. Include sources and limitations. These statements follow the record's website selection; private analysis files and source data are not automatically shared.
resultSaved: Result statement added to the draft. Save the record to retain it.
sourcePrivate: Supporting analysis retained privately; source files are not included in this edition.
reviewHelp: For each affected result, record why the retained result remains applicable to this edition. To omit or replace it, edit the record and prepare a new edition. This decision is pinned to this edition and its observed dependency revisions.
reviewSaving: Saving review decisions. This operation continues if the connection closes; reopen this edition to check its result.
reviewSaveFailed: The review decisions could not be saved. Check the operation result before retrying.
reviewSaveUncertain: The save was not confirmed. Your entered decisions remain here. Save again to recover the same operation and its result.
reviewSaved: Analysis review decisions saved for this edition.
reviewRequired: Resolve the analysis review decisions before exporting or publishing this edition.
resourceHelp: Each observation and expected-value comparison uses these saved limits for exact interpretation, boundary checks and margins. Input declarations also keep their own limits. Exceeding either limit stops preparation without replacing earlier results.
resourceLegacy: This comparison keeps its earlier interpretation. Enable declared limits to use sources with their own scalar policies in a new revision.
approximateEncoding: Exact encoding of value computed from approximate inputs
approximateEncodingHelp: Exact fractions preserve stored values and computed differences; they do not make approximate inputs mathematically exact or establish an error bound.
